description: Project housekeeping: Create proper README.md with project description/usage, requirements.txt with all dependencies, and .gitignore for Python projects. Also implement LinuxMonitorManager class in monitor_mode.py.
steps: Create a comprehensive README.md at the repo root covering: project name (POSFramework v2.1.0), description, features list, installation instructions (pip install -e .), usage examples for each CLI mode (recon, attack, full, analyze, export, terminal, gui), requirements (root/admin, wireless adapters), and platform support (Linux + Windows).
Create requirements.txt at the repo root listing: scapy, manuf, pyyaml (for upcoming config feature). These should match what setup.py already has plus the new YAML dependency.
Create .gitignore at the repo root with standard Python ignores: __pycache__/, *.pyc, *.pyo, .eggs/, *.egg-info/, dist/, build/, .env, .venv/, *.db, exports/, *.pcap, .idea/, .vscode/.

Implement LinuxMonitorManager class in posframework/monitor_mode.py that extends MonitorManagerInterface. It should: use 'iw' and 'ip' commands to enable/disable monitor mode, support channel setting via 'iw dev <iface> set channel <ch>', handle interface renaming (e.g., wlan0 -> wlan0mon), save/restore original state, implement get_mac_address using 'ip link show', implement set_mac_address using 'ip link set dev <iface> address <mac>'. Follow the same pattern as WindowsMonitorManager.

Update the module-level setup_monitor_mode() function in monitor_mode.py to auto-detect platform (IS_LINUX vs IS_WINDOWS) and use LinuxMonitorManager on Linux instead of always using WindowsChipMonitorManager.
Update posframework/recon.py to use the platform-appropriate monitor manager (use setup_monitor_mode which now handles both platforms).
acceptance_criteria: README.md exists with installation and usage documentation
requirements.txt exists with scapy, manuf, pyyaml listed
LinuxMonitorManager class exists in monitor_mode.py inheriting MonitorManagerInterface
LinuxMonitorManager implements all abstract methods (check_supported, enable_monitor_mode, disable_monitor_mode, set_channel, get_mac_address, set_mac_address)
setup_monitor_mode() function works on both Linux and Windows by detecting platform
verification: python -c "from posframework.monitor_mode import LinuxMonitorManager; print('LinuxMonitorManager imported OK')"
python -c "from posframework.monitor_mode import setup_monitor_mode; print('setup_monitor_mode imported OK')"
